title: Starting to get worried that it doesn't matter what game I build, it will be hated because AI.
author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
selftext:
Hello everyone. I've been building out my ideal RTS, and having a blast while doing it. It's truly incredible to me that I can think of a thing to add, and Claude/AI just adds it in. It means what was once a fantasy in terms of scope, is becoming a reality. Alright, it might not look amazing, but functionally it works. Beautifying comes later.

  
That being said! I have to admit, as fun as this project is, I am genuinely concerned that it doesn't matter how fun/good the game is to play, it won't matter because people will decry it as AI (ironically, a lot of those same people are chomping at the bit for the GTA6 rip. Ain't no human smart/fast enough on the planet to do that in the timeframe!), and it will just die a death.

I fully appreciate that could happen anyway because marketing. Urrrrrgh, don't even want to look at that problem yet. SIGH!

For context, I fully intend to release this game when I feel like it's a "proper" game, with enough of a  really enjoyable experience to give the player a bang for their buck.

All that to say, how do you peeps reconcile the excitement of building something you're genuinely proud of with the very real possibility that it'll be dismissed simply because you've used AI?

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: people find stuff to hate, stop worrying about it, if you make a game good enough most people will like it regardless.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body:
Thanks mate. Appreciate those kind works.

What's your experience been?

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: I have high standards and I'm building my own engine and tools, I'm not sharing much of anything online, let alone putting something on steam or something. If I do you won't know other then me honestly disclosing the usuage.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: Good to get your take. How honest/open will you be about AI usage? At the moment I'm intending (and I don't think this will change) of being totally honest. "This whole thing was made with AI" kind of stance.

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: Mine would be something  like "If you don't like AI do not play my game, if you can imagine it, I probably used it. Let others enjoy in peace"

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: So straight up hard ball? I kinda like that. No apologies. Ok, ok. Yeh.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: Mind if I DM you? I have further questions, if that's ok? No problem if not. I don't want to be a bother.

replies.author: Edenisb
replies.body: Yep I agree completely with you.

comments.author: PurpleManner5207
comments.body: people don't care if AI made or not. There is just a toxic loud minority spreading their bullshit believes that a developer had to work 5 years for effectively 1 cent per hour - and they would still shit on the game .

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: Thanks for saying, appreciated. That also made me laugh.

replies.author: HeleCritter
replies.body: Actually people don't even have to be loud about it. They just don't like to buy games that use AI in it and they don't have to tell anyone. That is simply just a part of their standards. You can't always please everyone.

replies.author: PurpleManner5207
replies.body: A study showed that 75% of players dont care at all if AI is sued or not. But a part of those 25% fuckers bomb every AI game so much you get the feeling everyone hates AI.

replies.author: HeleCritter
replies.body: Surveys can also be done with selection biases and if 75% of people don't care if AI is sued, then they're also the ones that just don't play AI games who don't really have to tell anyone about it. However, if you're referring to those 25%, there is also a chance that it's because of the lack of transparency not because of the AI itself.

comments.author: Time_Zombie_4431
comments.body: Just build and if it’s truly good people won’t care.

comments.author: Sozerius
comments.body:
You can consider that most of the people who complain about not getting traction (who I have seen, at least) don't have a great game even without the hate and would likely be passed over even if there was no AI. I know that might sting for some reading and I apologize for that. The message I mean to convey is that there is hope if you build real quality, so don't get down based on what people are saying about themselves.

Ive noticed a lot of cheap imitations and lesser experiences, nothing yet that is competitive with a human made project that would actually sell. But many that are competitive with human projects that dont sell. 

I'm not an anti. I love ai but the human behind it must make sure that it is a worthwhile experience AND that it is not a lesser version of something that already exists. Make it unique in a meaningful, non-conceptual way. There are a million RTS games but what can you add that makes it a new experience, basically is the question to ask yourself when considering if anyone else would be interested. There are a lot of ways to handle a question like this, from features to themes.

comments.author: TheRadishBros
comments.body: If the game is good, at least 80% of people won’t care. That’s probably lowballing it, tbh.

comments.author: ThreeDMK
comments.body:
I am build an AR iOS game over thanksgiving for the kids to race cars around the living room all evening with our phones. 

It’s a one shot.  People online would hate it.  They would be upset.

The kids are going to love it and likely remember the Thanksgiving for years.  

We pick our battles.  I choose not to care about how people online react to what I am building.  Years from now it won’t matter.  :)

comments.author: EastPlant1079
comments.body:
No, they literally expect better than mediocre, which games genuinely should be, if they are AI assisted. 

You can't just throw shit together and call it a game and upload it to Steam and expect humans to gobble up your hypothetical theoretical interpretation of what a game should be. 

And then to charge the same or even more than fully human-made stuff. Genuine insanity. 

Most people can genuinely buy a Claude or NEON subscription and make all your "games" for 20 bucks, with what they want inside it. 



Just make sure you'd play your own game for 40 + hours. That's the standard you need to put on yourself.

comments.author: PsychronicGames
comments.body: I wouldn't worry about it. I think when the dust settles, AI is just going to be a new way that everybody makes things and wont be looked down upon. This is a temporary era of adjustment. But when working on your project you may want to take your time, make sure the quality is good, don't rush it, but don't worry about using AI or not.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body:
Hmm. This is an interesting view. I think you're right in that the discourse will die down over time. Using that time to tune to nth degree is a valuable use of said time.

  
Thanks, really appreciate that. I'll bear that in mind.

comments.author: TorbenKoehn
comments.body: Just own it.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: Definitely. No point in trying to deny it. It'll be there on the Steam page for sure. Only fair to the person buying it.

comments.author: Brave_Bumblebee7565
comments.body: Don't care about what people say if it's not constructive feedback. A bit more sad may be to not get any feedback at all, but currently it's also expected :)

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: Fully expecting the latter, haha! Super hyped on release day....a month later and it's 3 purchases, 2 refunds, and the 1 that kept it is me. Wamp wamp!

replies.author: Brave_Bumblebee7565
replies.body: Yeah, that's the reality now, amount of content(music, books, games, soft) can be created by anybody now by far exceeds what people can consume

No one should expect making any money of anything they make with AI, and I could not care less as I'm having the blast of my life making games and software which I could only dream of before! 😍 🔥

comments.author: Woody_TLB
comments.body:
Just asked a similar thing today by myself.  
And like you, i am amazed by doing my stuff. I am a programmer, but i have started to use AI as tool, easy to get rid of boring stuff.

But after i asked similar thing, there were some replys and i can start a bit of a research about.   
And final result is:  
Stop reading this hate.  
Stop replying this hate.  
And don't get mad about hate when you share your thing, because in posting you get hate, but in for example link to your project you get fans and followers. And this don't even reply at your post, but they will use your link and informations.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body:
I think you're right, perhaps I'm getting too bogged down in the Reddit sphere of hate towards AI game development. It's a good point.

And noted on that last point. Hadn't considered that too hard, but will be now! Legend.

comments.author: Scott-Whittaker
comments.body:
Haters are going to hate. Do it because you love it and can’t *not* do it. But also don’t expect to make money from it. Hundreds of thousands of people are doing the same thing, both derivative slop and inspired unique gems from people realising their visions.

The hate will blow over. Frankly it’s economically infeasible to make games without AI in a world where AI exists. The best anyone can hope for is AI dev games with human art assets.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body:
You're so right about the passion for it. It's just so fun! Fortunately, this is exactly that, just a fun hobby for me. It's not something I'm going to need to rely on for money.

Interesting take in your last couple of sentences though, I completely agree. The economics of using AI are too hard to turn down for businesses already watching the margin lines.

replies.author: Scott-Whittaker
replies.body:
Yeah I’m in a weird place right now. I’m a web developer with over 20 years full stack web and app dev experience. I’ve been unemployed for the last 2 years. In that time I’ve spent a lot of time using Claude for a number of projects. 

It’s extremely compelling. In many ways I’ve never had so much fun or felt so free. But also there are no jobs. 

So now I’m making about 1/3 of minimum wage with a home 3D printing business and hoping to score a small contract or build something that people will pay money for. 

I’m fortunate enough that I have a small mortgage free house and no debt, so I can scrape by for a while. But not nearly enough for retirement and one medical emergency away from financial collapse. 

Interesting times.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body:
Surely with you knowledge you could build a really boring, but super useful, like...form filler or something? If you have 20 yrs experience in an industry, you must have noticed shit points. I work in Finance and my lord do I see opportunities for automation all the time. This is getting away from AI game dev now, but there's so much ripe ground. Sounds like you have loads of really interesting experience that could be drawn from.

Although, advertising. Woof. That's the real beast.

comments.author: Orchicon
comments.body: I think by the end of 2027, people will be more accepting. Every single day people start to become more accepting of AI for everything. The people who are haters now, will be praising things soon. Just keep at it and it will all work out in due time.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: Thanks mate, appreciate the kind words. And for what it's worth, I do agree with you. It's just bloody nerve wracking at the moment, haha!

This doesn't apply to the game "Big Walk" ;) Generally, you should do what you like, do what you like, in this case, the ideal RPG, and then you'll decide whether you want to spend time on marketing and promotion, or just play your game and have fun  :)

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body:
That's true, on both count. I guess honesty was the best policy in the example of Big Walk? I kinda of heard about it, but missed the main gripe. I heard it was well received originally though, so that's encouraging.

I looked at your profile, how's your game going?

Before they announced it, everyone was raving about how great the game was :) Thank you for your interest, I'm in the process of preparing two games, but I haven't had time to promote this one yet, but I like to play them sometimes :)

How is ur development going? Any good tips?

comments.author: HansVonMans
comments.body:
Maybe it helps to remember these three things:

- someone will always hate you for something
- even if some people hate you, some will appreciate you
- the thing people hate most is when something is liked

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body: Appreciate the words mate. I think I needed that lil confidence boost.

comments.author: Jason9mm
comments.body: There's plenty of AI hate, but it seems to be dimishing. Also there are now several examples of AI games having become a commercial hit. What you really should be worried about, if you hope to make any meaningful money, is the marketing and competition. Way more than 90% of games used to be utter commercial failures, and now that everyone and their mom is making games, there's going to be proportionally even less success stories. Most of the games by new developers like myself will be quite bad and would not have ever succeeded, but they do add to the noise, and more importantly some of them will be good and actual competition. None of these are of course reasons to not make and publish your game, but just be aware that finding any meaningful success is extremely hard.

replies.author: AMassiveFuckingTwat
replies.body:
I completely take what you're saying on board. I had a fantasy novel published through official means (I say official like it's a government stamp, it was a group that publsihes books on the regular), they advertised it through all of their channels and it flopped. The reviews/feedback I got was overwhelmingly positive in terms of the story/writing, but it was basically drowned out by the sheer volume of mass,  so I really do take your point on board.

Fortunately, I'm doing this just for shits and gigs. I'm very lucky in that I have a stable job, etc, so this is just a bit of fun.

Are you working on anything at the moment?

replies.author: Jason9mm
replies.body:
Cool, that's a fun and can't-go-too-much-wrong place to work from! And it really may help with coming up with good, unique stuff.

I have background in games, and I started vibe coding in around April. First I wanted to see if I could make a publishable game, so I made Type the World as a proof of concept / straightforward little game. It turned out pretty good and has sold a grand total of 9 units thus far, so largely in line with expectations.

Now that I know Claude is easily capable enough to provide what I want, I've started working on a more proper game I have more passion for, a turn based strategy game. I actually got a grant in 2025 for making a game concept, a part of which is this video: [https://vimeo.com/1107825416](https://vimeo.com/1107825416)

What I don't see a lot of in these discussions is the last part of "make game, release game, deal with emotions". Because it's real, and may surprise people who haven't gone through it before. I don't mean everyone's going to be crushed when their game flops, especially since a lot of people know that finding success is extremely unlikely. But even if your expectations are non-existent to low, it's going to feel like something. It always does, and some of it may come as a surprise. So, knowing that, I encourage everyone to create and release what they want, take it as it comes, and focus on the positive. And to keep going!

replies.author: StoneCypher

comments.author: NooneLikesYouBill

comments.author: dalonelygamer88

comments.author: AdSoggy8958

comments.author: Embergloam
comments.body:
I don't have much to add that hasn't already been said, but if you're truly building this with heart, players will feel it. The dismissive-because-AI crowd is going to have a hard time finding much of anything in the near future that wasn't at least AI-assisted in some way.

AI is one of those inflection points where everything changes. It reminds me of the internet taking off during my pre-teen and teen years. People were skeptical then, too, and it ended up reshaping the world.
